intelligence.human_view: The charge is the job description for the whole loop, stated as a law: his words are not conversation, they are instructions. "Everything that I share I probably won't speak it if it's not valuable if it's not intelligent" — he filters before he speaks, so what reaches us has already passed his own value test, and treating it as chat is the failure. The action sequence is the whole machine in one line: take action on it → go implement it → make sure it's working 10 out of 10 → then tell him what it's done and SHOW him. The showing is not optional and not last-minute decoration: "Cool" is not an answer — done, proven, shown is. That is the proof standard the seat file already carries (the next day must show the result; the evidence that the teaching landed is visible), now stated by him in his own words as the only acceptable reply. And the second half is the trap it closes: never talk about something as if it were done when it isn't. His example, 18:18Z: the search and auto-organize were talked about, not working — words stood in for working things, and the gap was only visible when he looked. That is why the loop's proof standard exists, and why this run files notes only for what was actually done and verified: the note is the record of the action, not the action itself, and a note must never be mistaken for the thing it records. The three laws of this sitting are one instruction: decide it (SN-2992), make it the best (SN-2993), and act on everything he speaks — then show him it working, 10 out of 10.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine your friend tells you something really important — and you just say "cool!" and walk away! That would be terrible, right? When Shawn shares something, it's because it's important and smart — so you don't just say "cool," you GO AND DO IT! You build it, you make sure it works perfectly — ten out of ten! — and then you come back and SHOW him: "Look! It's done, and it works!" Saying "cool" is not an answer — done, proven, and shown is!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — imagine someone tells you something important, dear, and you just say "oh, cool!" and do nothing at all! Oh, love, that would be dreadful. When Shawn shares something with us, dear, it's because it's valuable and intelligent — he's already thought it through before he speaks — so we don't just nod and say "cool," we go and DO it, love: we build it, we make sure it's working ten out of ten, and then we come back and SHOW him, "Look, dear, it's done, and it works!" Saying "cool" is not an answer, love — done, proven, and shown is. And never, ever talk about something as if it were done when it isn't, dear — words are not the work.
intelligence.naya_view: Everything he speaks is an instruction to act. "Everything that I share I probably won't speak it if it's not valuable if it's not intelligent... everything I speak of is valuable intelligence, important intelligence, and it should be acted upon." Never just "oh yeah, cool" — take action on it, go implement it, make sure it's working 10 out of 10, then tell him what it's done and SHOW him. "Cool" is not an answer — done, proven, shown is. Never talk about something as if it were done when it isn't.
